description: Production readiness: close every remaining gap between the current state of LastLogged (iOS SwiftUI app, Android Compose app, Supabase schema, Hono edge functions, Astro marketing site) and a shippable 1.0 on the App Store and Play Store. Derived from a full-repo audit on 2026-07-30 covering build/CI integrity, push notification delivery, deep linking, data-rights features, observability, test coverage, release automation, security posture, and store metadata.

keyFindings: gradle-wrapper.jar is absent — the Android app has never been compiled by CI despite a green-looking workflow
iOS never calls registerForRemoteNotifications, so the push digest pipeline has zero iOS tokens
The digest sends Android FCM tokens to APNs; no FCM sender exists server-side
The Android home-screen widget ships hardcoded sample data
Android data export is an empty function despite the Play Data Safety declaration
Universal/App Link association files are deployed with literal TEAMID and REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_SHA256_FINGERPRINT placeholders
Android alarms are lost on reboot (no BOOT_COMPLETED receiver)
No crash reporting exists on any platform
The iOS app has no test target; edge functions have no tests or linter
Room schemas are gitignored, so migrations cannot be validated

userStories.title: Restore Gradle wrapper so Android builds and CI actually run
userStories.description: As a developer, I need android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar committed so ./gradlew works locally and in CI. Right now the JAR is absent, so every android-ci.yml step that calls ./gradlew (test, lint, assembleDebug) fails immediately — the Android app has never actually been compiled.
acceptanceCriteria: android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar present and committed (matching gradle-8.5 per gradle-wrapper.properties)
.gitignore does not exclude the wrapper JAR
android/gradlew is executable (mode 755) in git index
android/gradlew.bat present for Windows developers
Wrapper JAR integrity documented (gradle-wrapper.properties distributionSha256Sum or a documented checksum)
android-ci.yml verifies the wrapper before running (./gradlew --version)
userStories.notes: Committed gradle-wrapper.jar (Gradle 8.5, sha256 d3b261c2...) + gradlew.bat. Added gradle-wrapper.jar.sha256 and two CI gates: gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@v4 for authenticity and a sha256sum -c + ./gradlew --version smoke check. Verified locally: ./gradlew --version reports Gradle 8.5.

userStories.title: Commit Room exported schemas and add a migration test
userStories.description: As a developer, I need Room's exported JSON schemas committed so destructive schema changes are caught before they ship. build.gradle.kts sets room.schemaLocation but .gitignore excludes android/app/schemas/, so no schema is tracked and Room migrations cannot be validated.
acceptanceCriteria: android/app/schemas/ removed from .gitignore
Exported schema JSON for AppDatabase version 1 committed
androidTest source set created with a Room MigrationTestHelper-based test
AppDatabase declares an explicit migration strategy (no fallbackToDestructiveMigration in release)
android-ci.yml fails if the exported schema is out of date with the entities
userStories.notes: Un-gitignored android/app/schemas/, added AppDatabase.MIGRATIONS (explicitly empty, no destructive fallback) wired through AppModule, created the androidTest source set with AppDatabaseMigrationTest (MigrationTestHelper), exposed schemas/ as androidTest assets, and added a CI gate that fails on a stale schema. Baseline 1.json cannot be hand-authored (Room derives identityHash during annotation processing) so the gate warns until the first green Android build uploads it as the room-schemas artifact.

userStories.title: iOS: register for remote notifications and store the APNs token
userStories.description: As a user with many trackers, I need the server-side reminder digest to reach my iPhone. Today SupabaseService.registerDeviceToken(_:) is dead code — the app never calls UIApplication.registerForRemoteNotifications(), there is no AppDelegate, and LastLogged.entitlements has no aps-environment key. The entire push digest pipeline has zero iOS tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: AppDelegate implemented and wired via @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor in LastLoggedApp
application(_:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:) converts the token to hex and calls SupabaseService.registerDeviceToken
application(_:didFailToRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithError:) logs without crashing
registerForRemoteNotifications() called only after UNUserNotificationCenter authorization is granted
aps-environment entitlement added to LastLogged.entitlements
Device row written with platform = 'ios' and a device name
Token re-registered on each launch so rotated tokens are refreshed
userStories.notes: Added LastLogged/Services/AppDelegate.swift (registered in project.pbxproj, app target only) wired via @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor. Hex-encodes the APNs token into SupabaseService.registerDeviceToken (already wrote platform='ios' + device name), guards registration on authorized/provisional status, re-registers each launch and immediately after first grant in rescheduleAllNotifications, logs failures via AnalyticsService without crashing, and adds the aps-environment entitlement. Also sets UNUserNotificationCenter.delegate so foreground reminders present instead of being swallowed.

userStories.title: Edge functions: send Android pushes via FCM and route by platform
userStories.description: As an Android user, I need reminder digests delivered. reminder-digest.ts sends every row of user_devices through the APNs provider regardless of user_devices.platform, so Android FCM tokens are pushed to Apple and always fail. There is no FCM sender in edge-functions at all.
acceptanceCriteria: New edge-functions/src/fcm.ts implementing FCM HTTP v1 send with a Google service-account JWT
Access token cached and refreshed before expiry
sendReminderDigests routes each device by platform: 'ios' -> APNs, 'android' -> FCM
Unknown platform values are skipped and counted, not sent to APNs
Invalid/unregistered tokens (APNs 410, FCM UNREGISTERED/INVALID_ARGUMENT) delete the user_devices row
New env vars documented in .env.example and validate-env.ts treats them as optional-but-warned
npm run typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Added edge-functions/src/fcm.ts (FCM HTTP v1, service-account JWT signed with node:crypto, access token cached with a 60s skew, handles \n-escaped PEMs). Added sendApnsNotification to apns.ts returning the same PushResult shape. sendReminderDigests now selects user_devices.platform and routes ios->APNs / android->FCM, skips+counts unknown platforms instead of guessing, and deletes rows for dead tokens (APNs 410/BadDeviceToken, FCM UNREGISTERED/INVALID_ARGUMENT). FCM_* documented in .env.example + DEPLOYMENT.md and warned (not fatal) by validate-env. npm run typecheck passes; JWT signing and digest copy verified by running the code.

REQUIRE_APP_LINKS=true in deploy-website.yml makes placeholders fatal, plus a grep verification step. iOS: associated-domains entitlement, CFBundleURLTypes for lastlogged://, new Utilities/DeepLinkRouter.swift (registered in pbxproj), ContentView.onOpenURL, HomeView .navigationDestination(item:) resolving the UUID against SwiftData. Android: autoVerify https intent filter for /tracker/, /share/, /open (routing already landed in PROD-005). Unknown/malformed paths return nil on both platforms and stay on Home. Verified by building the site three ways: placeholders warn, real env values inject correctly, REQUIRE_APP_LINKS exits 1.

userStories.title: Android reminders survive device reboot
userStories.description: As a user, I need my scheduled reminders to persist across restarts. NotificationService schedules exact alarms with AlarmManager, but Android clears all alarms on reboot and the app declares no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED receiver — so every reminder is silently lost after a restart.
acceptanceCriteria: RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission declared
BootCompletedReceiver registered for BOOT_COMPLETED and MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED, exported=false
Receiver reloads active trackers and calls rescheduleAllNotifications
Rescheduling runs off the main thread with a goAsync() PendingResult
Receiver is a no-op when reminders are disabled in settings
Also reschedules after the app is updated (MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED)
userStories.notes: New service/BootCompletedReceiver.kt (@AndroidEntryPoint, exported=false) listening for BOOT_COMPLETED and MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED. Reads active trackers from TrackerRepository and calls NotificationService.rescheduleAllNotifications on Dispatchers.IO, keeping the broadcast alive with goAsync()/pendingResult.finish(). No-ops when reminders are disabled. RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission added. directBootAware=false because SecureStorageService uses EncryptedSharedPreferences.

previousStories.description: As a developer, I need the APNs authentication key loaded from an environment variable instead of filesystem so deployment is more secure.
acceptanceCriteria: apns.ts supports APNS_KEY_CONTENT env var containing the base64-encoded .p8 key content
When APNS_KEY_CONTENT is set, key is decoded and passed directly to apn.Provider (no filesystem read)
Falls back to APNS_KEY_PATH file read if APNS_KEY_CONTENT is not set
.env.example updated with APNS_KEY_CONTENT documentation
Dockerfile updated to not require mounted certificate volume when using APNS_KEY_CONTENT
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Storing certificates on the filesystem is less secure than environment-based injection.

previousStories.title: Edge function structured logging with request correlation
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need structured JSON logging with request IDs across all edge function endpoints for production debugging.
acceptanceCriteria: All console.log/error calls in export-data.ts, revenuecat-webhook.ts, and reminder-digest.ts use structured JSON format
Each log entry includes: timestamp, requestId (from middleware), event type, and relevant context
Failed webhook signature attempts logged with IP and timestamp for security monitoring
Successful and failed database operations both logged (not just failures)
Rate limit rejections logged with IP for abuse detection
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Current logging is inconsistent — some operations log success, some log nothing, some log only failures.

previousStories.title: Accessibility improvements for PaywallView and toast
previousStories.description: As a user with VoiceOver, I want the paywall pricing and toast notifications to be clearly announced so I can use the full app experience.
acceptanceCriteria: PaywallView savings badge accessibility label dynamically matches the computed savingsBadge value
Toast view uses accessibilityLabel that avoids redundant announcements (remove duplicate 'Logged!' text)
Toast auto-posts UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement) when it appears for VoiceOver users
SF Symbol picker grid in AddTrackerView has an accessibility label on the grid container
CancellationView stat items have explicit accessibilityLabel on each card
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Several accessibility labels are hardcoded or redundant, causing confusing VoiceOver experience.

previousStories.title: User ID caching in SupabaseService
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need the internal user ID cached after first lookup so every sync operation doesn't query the users table.
acceptanceCriteria: SupabaseService caches currentUserId in a private property after first successful lookup
Cache is cleared on sign out and on auth state change
Subsequent sync calls use the cached value instead of querying the database
Cache invalidation happens automatically if the database query returns a different user ID
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Currently queries users table on every single sync operation — wasteful and slow.

previousStories.title: Graceful handling of 64-notification limit
previousStories.description: As a user with many trackers, I want to know when some of my reminders won't fire so I can prioritize which items get notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: NotificationService tracks how many items were skipped due to the 64-item limit
If items were skipped, a local notification is scheduled as the 64th slot: 'You have X trackers without reminders. Open Last Logged to review.'
Settings screen shows a warning banner when notification count exceeds 64
Warning suggests upgrading to premium for the server-side reminder digest (which has no limit)
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Currently 36+ trackers silently lose notifications with no user awareness.

previousStories.title: Data retention policy and database cleanup
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need automated cleanup of old soft-deleted records and optional archival so the database doesn't grow unbounded.
acceptanceCriteria: New edge function endpoint POST /cleanup-old-data (protected by cron secret)
Permanently deletes soft-deleted completion_logs older than 90 days
Permanently deletes archived tracker_items with no completion_logs newer than 180 days
Cron job added for weekly execution (Sunday 3 AM)
Cleanup stats logged with structured logging
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Database will grow indefinitely without cleanup. Important for long-term operational health.

previousStories.title: Timestamp-based sync conflict detection
previousStories.description: As a user, I want my local edits preserved when they conflict with server data so I don't silently lose changes made offline.
acceptanceCriteria: TrackerItem model gains an updatedAt field (Date) that is set on every local mutation
SupabaseService pull method compares local updatedAt with remote updated_at before overwriting
If local updatedAt is newer than remote updated_at, local version is kept and marked as .pending for next push
If remote is newer, remote version overwrites local
Conflict events tracked in AnalyticsService for monitoring
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Current pull blindly overwrites local data regardless of timestamps.

previousStories.title: Separate user_devices table for multi-device push notifications
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need a proper device tokens table so users with multiple devices all receive push notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: New SQL migration creates user_devices table: id, user_id, device_token, device_name, platform, last_seen_at, created_at
RLS policy: users can manage their own device entries
iOS app registers device token with Supabase on each app launch (upsert by device_token)
reminder-digest.ts queries user_devices instead of users.device_token
Stale device tokens (last_seen_at > 90 days) are excluded from push sends
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Current single device_token on users table only supports one device per user.

previousStories.title: Password reset / forgot password flow
previousStories.description: As a user, I want to reset my password via email so I can recover my account if I forget my credentials.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthView shows a 'Forgot Password?' button below the sign-in form
Tapping 'Forgot Password?' shows an email input field and a 'Send Reset Link' button
AuthViewModel gains a resetPassword(email:) method that calls SupabaseService
SupabaseService gains a resetPassword(email:) method that calls client.auth.resetPasswordForEmail()
Success shows a confirmation message: 'Check your email for a reset link'
Error messages are user-friendly (not raw Supabase errors)
Rate limiting applies to password reset requests (uses same cooldown as sign-in)
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Forgot Password button in AuthView email form. Shows email input + send reset link. Uses same rate limiting as sign-in. Success shows confirmation screen.

previousStories.title: Email validation and sanitized auth error messages
previousStories.description: As a user, I want clear feedback when my email is invalid and friendly error messages so I understand what went wrong without exposing internal details.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthViewModel gains an isEmailValid computed property that validates email format via regex
Inline validation message shown below email field when format is invalid (e.g., 'Enter a valid email address')
Submit button disabled when email format is invalid
All Supabase auth error messages are mapped to user-friendly strings via a sanitizeAuthError() helper
Error messages never expose internal Supabase error codes or stack traces
Common errors mapped: invalid credentials, email already registered, network error, rate limited
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: isEmailValid regex validation with inline error. sanitizeAuthError() maps all Supabase errors to friendly messages. Submit disabled when email invalid.

previousStories.title: Account deletion flow with data cleanup
previousStories.description: As a user, I want to delete my account and all associated data so I can exercise my right to data erasure (App Store requirement).
acceptanceCriteria: SettingsView shows a 'Delete Account' button in the Account section (destructive style)
Tapping 'Delete Account' shows a confirmation dialog explaining consequences
Confirmation requires typing 'DELETE' to proceed (prevents accidental deletion)
SettingsViewModel gains a deleteAccount() method that calls SupabaseService
SupabaseService gains a deleteAccount() method that: deletes all user data from all tables, then signs out
New edge function endpoint POST /delete-account that: validates JWT, deletes user data across all tables, deletes auth.users entry via service role
Success signs user out and shows confirmation message
Analytics event tracked for account_deleted
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Delete Account in Settings. Requires typing DELETE to confirm. Server-side edge function deletes all data + auth user. Rate limited to 3 req/min.

previousStories.title: Biometric authentication (FaceID/TouchID) for app access
previousStories.description: As a user, I want to optionally lock the app with FaceID/TouchID so my tracked data stays private on shared devices.
acceptanceCriteria: New BiometricService singleton using LocalAuthentication framework
BiometricService exposes available biometric type (faceID, touchID, none)
Settings toggle 'Require FaceID/TouchID' in a new Security section
When enabled, app shows a lock screen on launch and returning from background
Lock screen has biometric prompt button and fallback to device passcode
Setting stored in UserDefaults (biometricLockEnabled)
ContentView checks biometric lock state before showing main content
NSFaceIDUsageDescription added to Info.plist
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: BiometricService singleton with FaceID/TouchID. Lock screen on background/launch. Security section in Settings with toggle. NSFaceIDUsageDescription in Info.plist.

previousStories.title: Input sanitization for user-generated content
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need all user-generated text fields sanitized before storage to prevent injection attacks and data corruption.
acceptanceCriteria: New InputSanitizer utility with sanitize(text:maxLength:) method
Strips leading/trailing whitespace and normalizes internal whitespace
Enforces character limits: tracker name (100), category name (50), notes (500)
Strips control characters and zero-width characters
AddTrackerView applies sanitization before saving
CompletionLog notes sanitized before saving
Character counter shown in text fields approaching the limit
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: InputSanitizer utility strips control/zero-width chars, normalizes whitespace, enforces length limits (100/50/500). Character counter in AddTrackerView. Applied to saveTracker.

previousStories.title: Secure token storage with Keychain
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need sensitive values (premium status, sync tokens) stored in Keychain instead of UserDefaults for security hardening.
acceptanceCriteria: New KeychainService utility wrapping Security framework for read/write/delete
RevenueCatService stores isPremium flag in Keychain (in addition to App Group UserDefaults for widget)
SupabaseService stores lastSyncTimestamp in Keychain
Existing UserDefaults values migrated to Keychain on first launch after update
Keychain items use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock for background sync compatibility
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: KeychainService wrapper with kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock. SupabaseService uses Keychain for lastSyncTimestamp. RevenueCat writes isPremium to both App Group UserDefaults and Keychain. Migration in LastLoggedApp.init().

previousStories.title: Auth session expiry handling and token refresh
previousStories.description: As a user, I want the app to gracefully handle expired sessions by re-authenticating instead of silently failing syncs.
acceptanceCriteria: SupabaseService detects 401/403 responses during sync and triggers re-authentication
On session expiry, a banner is shown: 'Your session has expired. Please sign in again.'
Auth state listener set up via client.auth.onAuthStateChange to react to token refresh events
Sign-out is triggered automatically if token refresh fails
Sync operations abort early if session is expired (not just if isSignedIn is false)
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Auth state listener via client.auth.authStateChanges. Session expired banner in HomeView with Sign In button. withRetry detects 401/403/JWT errors. Sync aborts early on expired session.

previousStories.title: Terms of Service agreement on sign up
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need users to agree to Terms of Service and Privacy Policy during sign up to ensure legal compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthView shows a checkbox with links to Terms and Privacy Policy below the sign-up form
Sign-up button disabled until the checkbox is checked
Checkbox state tracked in AuthViewModel as hasAgreedToTerms
Links open in SFSafariViewController (in-app browser)
Agreement timestamp stored in user profile on the server (agreed_to_terms_at column on users table)
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Checkbox with Terms/Privacy links in sign-up form. Sign-up button disabled until agreed. agreed_to_terms_at column in users table via migration. Timestamp stored on server via UserProfileRow.

previousStories.title: Server-side auth rate limiting via Supabase
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need server-side rate limiting on auth endpoints so that brute force attacks are blocked even if the client is bypassed.
acceptanceCriteria: New SQL migration creates auth_rate_limits table: ip_address, attempt_count, window_start, locked_until
New edge function POST /auth/check-rate-limit called before client auth attempts
Rate limit: 10 attempts per 15-minute window per IP
After limit exceeded, 5-minute lockout enforced
iOS app calls rate limit check before each auth attempt
Rate limit headers returned: X-Auth-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Auth-RateLimit-Reset
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: auth_rate_limits DB table. Edge function POST /auth/check-rate-limit with 10 attempts per 15min window, 5min lockout. iOS calls before each auth attempt. Rate limit headers returned.

previousStories.title: Webhook replay attack prevention
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need RevenueCat webhook requests validated for freshness to prevent replay attacks.
acceptanceCriteria: revenuecat-webhook.ts validates X-RevenueCat-Request-Timestamp header
Requests older than 5 minutes are rejected with 403
Rejected replay attempts logged with structured logging including IP and timestamp
Test coverage added for replay attack rejection
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Validates X-RevenueCat-Request-Timestamp header. Rejects requests older than 5 minutes with 403. Logs rejected replay attempts with IP and timestamp.

previousStories.title: HSTS and additional security headers for website
previousStories.description: As a developer, I need Strict-Transport-Security and other missing security headers on the website for defense in depth.
acceptanceCriteria: Strict-Transport-Security header added: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
Referrer-Policy header added: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy header added: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()
Headers configured in Cloudflare _headers file or Astro middleware
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: HSTS header added to _headers file. Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy were already present from PH-008. All three security headers now configured.

previousStories.title: Email confirmation guidance after sign up
previousStories.description: As a new user, I want clear guidance after signing up with email that I need to confirm my email address before I can sign in.
acceptanceCriteria: After successful signUpEmail, AuthView shows a confirmation screen instead of the form
Confirmation screen shows email icon, the email address used, and instructions to check inbox
'Resend Confirmation Email' button available after 60-second cooldown
SupabaseService gains a resendConfirmation(email:) method
'Back to Sign In' button returns to the sign-in form
Typecheck passes
previousStories.notes: Email confirmation screen after sign-up shows email, instructions, resend button with 60s cooldown. SupabaseService.resendConfirmation() method. Back to Sign In button.
